summaryTr: The presidential office's policy chief promoted from within signals intent to maintain existing policy direction.

editorials.bodyTr: The president's promotion of Ha Jun-kyung, senior secretary for economic growth, to chief of presidential policy staff has been interpreted as signaling a continuation of existing policy directions. summaryTr: Shinhan Bank suffers data breach affecting 25,000 customers through authentication bypass hacking
Chinese-language AI infiltration tool traces found, raising possibilities of AI-enabled hacking
KB and Hana Bank also hit by similar attacks, urgent need for enhanced security at financial institutions
editorials.bodyTr: Personal information belonging to 25,000 customers at Shinhan Bank has been leaked through a hacking attack that bypassed authentication measures. Chinese language traces found on the servers used in the attack suggest the use of an AI autonomous penetration tool, raising concerns about AI-enabled hacking. Similar leaks have been confirmed at KB Kookmin Bank and Hana Bank, prompting authorities and financial institutions to strengthen vulnerable services and enhance real-time monitoring.

editorial.title: [사설] DMZ 지뢰 폭발, ‘불의의 사고’ 아닌 ‘북한의 도발’이다
editorial.body: 입력 업데이트 종합 26면 이재명 대통령은 어제(1일) 국군의날 기념식에서 열흘 전 우리 장병 3명이 북한이 비무장지대(DMZ)에 매설한 지뢰 폭발로 중경상을 입은 사건을 언급하며 “불의의 사고”라고 표현했다. 북한의 정전협정 위반에 대한 규탄도 없었고, 김여정 노동당 부장의 ‘자작극’ 주장에 대한 반박도 없었다. 대신 이 대통령은 “정부는 남북 간 군사적 긴장을 낮추기 위한 실질적인 조치를 일관되게 이어 나가겠다”고 밝혔다. 합동참모본부와 유엔군사령부가 29일 최근 서부전선에서 발생한 지뢰 폭발 사건 추가 현장 조사를 진행하며 발견한 북한 수지(플라스틱) 반보병 지뢰. 뉴스1 우선 이 대통령의 발언은 그제 북한의 정전협정 위반을 공식화한 합참과 유엔사의 입장과 배치된다는 점을 지적하지 않을 수 없다. 합참은 ‘국경선 요새화’ 등 한반도 긴장을 고조시키는 활동의 즉각 중단과 함께 북측의 사과와 책임 있는 조치를 강력히 촉구했다. 만약 이런 요구에 응하지 않으면 향후 군사적 대응에 나설 것이라고 경고했다. 군사 대응을 경고한 것은 북한이 DMZ에 지뢰를 매설한 행위를 불법적인 정전협정 위반 행위이자 도발 행위로 판단하고 있기 때문이다. 그런데 정작 군 통수권자인 이 대통령은 합참의 경고와 맞지 않는 발언을 한 것이다. 이번 사고는 ‘불의의 사고’가 아니라 지뢰 매설이란 도발 행위에 의해 일어난 결과다. 지뢰는 상대방에게 위해를 가하려는 목적으로 매설한다. 북한 관할 구역에 매설했다면 방어용이란 명분이 통하겠지만, 비무장지대에서 그런 일을 한 것은 명백한 도발이다. 왜 도발을 도발이라 규정하지 못하는가. 더구나 한반도의 군사적 긴장을 고조시키는 측은 우리가 아니라 북한이란 점이 이번에 재확인됐다. 군사적 긴장을 낮추는 노력은 북한이 해야 할 일이고, 백번 양보해도 남북이 함께해야 한다. 국경 요새화란 명목으로 군사 긴장을 고조시키는 북한의 도발에 의해 명백한 피해가 발생했고, 앞으로도 일어날 수 있는데도 우리 한쪽만 긴장을 낮추는 조치를 하겠다는 대북 접근법에 공감하는 국민이 얼마나 될지 의문이다. 얼마 전 국회에서 DMZ 지뢰 폭발 당시 아비규환의 현장에서 다친 중사가 부대원들에게 자신보다 더 많이 다친 대대장을 챙기라고 명령한 뒤 사고 현장을 기어서 탈출하는 모습이 담긴 보디캠 영상이 공개됐다. 과연 북한 도발로 부상당한 전우를 지켜본 이들에게 대통령의 발언이 어떻게 들렸을지 생각했으면 한다.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] DMZ Mine Blast Is North Korea's Provocation, Not an Accident
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung describes DMZ landmine explosion as 'unintended accident,' sparking controversy
Joint Chiefs of Staff and UN Command defined it as North Korean provocation violating armistice agreement, at odds with presidential stance
Critics question whether president's emphasis on reducing tensions in front of wounded soldiers from North Korean provocation is appropriate
editorial.bodyTr:
President Lee Jae-myung referred to the incident in which three Korean soldiers were seriously injured by landmines planted by North Korea in the demilitarized zone ten days ago as an "unforeseen accident" during yesterday's Armed Forces Day ceremony. There was no condemnation of North Korea's violation of the armistice agreement, nor any rebuttal to Kim Yo-jong's claims of a "false flag operation." Instead, President Lee stated, "The government will consistently implement substantive measures to reduce military tensions between the North and South."

First, it must be pointed out that the president's remarks contradict the position of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the United Nations Command, which officially confirmed North Korea's violation of the armistice agreement the day before. The JCS strongly demanded that North Korea immediately cease activities escalating tensions on the Korean Peninsula, including "fortifying border areas," and called for an apology and responsible measures from the North. It also warned that if these demands are not met, South Korea will take military countermeasures. The military warning was issued because the placement of landmines in the DMZ is deemed an illegal violation of the armistice agreement and a provocation.

Yet the commander-in-chief himself made remarks inconsistent with the JCS's warning. This incident was not an "unforeseen accident" but a consequence resulting from the provocative act of planting mines. Mines are laid with the intention of causing harm to the other side. Had they been placed in North Korean territory, a defensive justification could be offered, but doing so in the demilitarized zone is clearly a provocation. Why can the government not call a provocation what it is?

Moreover, this incident has reconfirmed that it is North Korea, not South Korea, that is escalating military tensions on the Korean Peninsula. Reducing military tensions is North Korea's responsibility, and at the very least, it is something South and North must undertake together. Given that clear casualties have already occurred from North Korea's provocation in the guise of "border fortification" and more could happen, one must question how many citizens will support an approach toward North Korea that involves only one side taking measures to ease tensions.

Recently, bodycam footage was released in the National Assembly showing a sergeant who was injured during the chaotic scene of the DMZ landmine explosion ordering his fellow soldiers to attend to their more severely injured battalion commander before crawling away from the site himself. I would hope the president would consider how those who witnessed their comrades wounded by North Korean provocation heard his remarks.

editorial.title: Fact vs. fiction
editorial.body: A controversial film hypothesis raises questions about historical distortion Controversy over “The Assassin(s),” a film about the 1974 shooting death of Yuk Young-soo, wife of then-President Park Chung-hee, has spilled into the political arena. At issue is not artistic license itself, but whether cinematic invention can justify distorting established historical facts. The film depicts the Aug. 15, 1974, shooting and advances a plot hypothesis that people close to Park or the Korean Central Intelligence Agency may have been involved. The filmmakers insist they did not explicitly identify who was behind the assassination. Yet the film invites audiences to entertain the insinuation that Park himself used or was involved in the incident to overcome a political crisis. For his children, the suggestion that their father may have been involved in their mother’s death to preserve his power is an especially grave insult. The historical record does not substantiate the theory. The Special Investigation Headquarters concluded at the time that Moon Se-kwang, acting on orders from North Korea and Jochongnyeon, the pro-Pyongyang federation of Korean residents in Japan, attempted to assassinate Park but missed, with a stray bullet striking and killing the first lady. Questions have been raised over the years, but no evidence has emerged to substantiate the claim that Park orchestrated his wife’s death. Rep. Joo Jin-woo of the opposition People Power Party criticized the film for portraying Park, rather than North Korea, as being behind Yuk’s assassination. He called it a historical distortion, not mere cinematic imagination, and said those involved should be punished. Party leader Jang Dong-hyeok called for a boycott, while Rep. Shin Dong-uk urged that screenings be halted. A former Seoul city council member also filed a criminal complaint against some production staff, accusing them of defaming Park. Yet the ruling Democratic Party of Korea has remained conspicuously silent. Why? Perhaps because the film is doing for the party what it has long done itself: denigrating Park. If a film had used a similarly shocking imagination to disparage former Presidents Kim Dae-jung or Roh Moo-hyun, would the Democratic Party have been so tolerant? It is difficult to imagine it would have been. The party pushed through a law imposing up to five years in prison for spreading false information about the May 18 Democratization Movement, which took place in its traditional stronghold of Jeonnam-Gwangju. Yet when a film raises an unverified theory about Park, the party has nothing to say. The contrast is glaring. It is a double standard. The controversy also recalls the uproar over the Paichai High School baseball team’s “Let’s go to Starbucks” chant during a June 29 game. President Lee Jae Myung lashed out at Starbucks Korea, displaying his remarkable “imagination” by linking its “Tank Day” tumbler promotion for May 18, 2026, with an insult to the May 18 Democratization Movement of 1980. Many saw this as an excessive leap in logic. Nevertheless, some government ministries went so far as to launch a boycott. Chung Yong-jin, chairman of Shinsegae Group, Starbucks Korea’s parent company, apologized publicly, while police conducted a search and seizure at Starbucks Korea. The Seoul-based Paichai team then visited the May 18 National Cemetery in Jeonnam-Gwangju to apologize for its chant. By the same standard, the film’s director, actors and other production staff should at least be prepared to visit Park Chung-hee’s grave, pay their respects and apologize. There is a serious danger when unverified hypotheses become embedded in the public consciousness as hidden truths through the power of a polished commercial film. Cinematic imagination is no substitute for evidence. When fiction is presented as a plausible explanation of established historical facts, especially a national tragedy, criticism of historical distortion is inevitable. Freedom of expression matters. But it is not a license to blur the line between fact and fiction. summaryTr: 1974년 한국 역대 첫 영부인 암살사건을 다룬 영화가 증거 부족에도 불구하고 박 대통령이 아내의 죽음을 주도했을 가능성에 대한 추측을 불러일으키고 있다.

1974년 박정희 당시 대통령의 부인 육영수 저격 사망 사건을 다룬 영화 '암살자(들)'을 둘러싼 논란이 정치권으로 번져나갔다. 문제는 예술적 자유 자체가 아니라, 영화적 창작이 확립된 역사적 사실을 왜곡할 정당성이 있는가 하는 점이다. 이 영화는 1974년 8월 15일의 저격 사건을 묘사하고, 박 전 대통령 측근 인물들이나 중앙정보부가 관여했을 수 있다는 음모론을 제시한다. 제작진은 암살의 배후자를 명시적으로 지목하지 않았다고 주장하지만, 영화는 관객들에게 박 전 대통령이 정치적 위기를 극복하기 위해 이 사건을 이용했거나 관여했을 가능성을 암시하도록 유도한다. 박 전 대통령의 자녀들에게 아버지가 권력 유지를 위해 어머니의 죽음에 관여했을 수 있다는 암시는 특히 심각한 모욕이다. 역사 기록은 이 같은 이론을 뒷받침하지 않는다. 당시 특별수사본부는 문세광이 북한과 재일본조국평화통일촉진회의 지시를 받아 박 전 대통령을 암살하려다 실패했으며, 유탄에 영부인이 맞아 사망했다는 결론을 내렸다. 수년간 여러 의문이 제기되어 왔지만, 박 전 대통령이 부인의 죽음을 주도했다는 주장을 뒷받침할 증거는 나타나지 않았다.

국민의힘 주진우 의원은 이 영화가 북한이 아닌 박 전 대통령을 육영수 암살의 배후로 묘사한다며 비판했다. 그는 이를 영화적 상상력이 아닌 역사 왜곡이라 지적했고, 관련자들을 처벌해야 한다고 주장했다. 당 지도부인 장동혁 대표는 불매운동을 촉구했고, 신동욱 의원은 상영 중단을 촉구했다. 전직 서울시의원도 제작진을 상대로 박 전 대통령 명예훼손 혐의로 고소했다. 그러나 여당인 더불어민주당은 눈에 띄게 침묵을 지키고 있다. 왜일까? 아마도 이 영화가 자신들이 오랫동안 해온 일을 하고 있기 때문일 것이다. 즉, 박 전 대통령을 폄훼하는 것이다. 만약 어떤 영화가 유사하게 충격적인 상상력으로 김대중이나 노무현 전 대통령을 폄훼했다면, 민주당이 이토록 관대했을까? 그럴 리 없다. 민주당은 전라남도·광주라는 기반 지역에서 일어난 5·18 민주화운동에 관해 거짓 정보를 유포할 경우 최대 5년의 징역형을 규정하는 법안을 통과시켰다. 그런데 박 전 대통령에 관해 검증되지 않은 이론을 제기하는 영화에 대해서는 아무 말도 없다. 대조가 선명하다. 이는 이중 잣대다.

이번 논란은 6월 29일 경기 배재고 야구팀의 "스타벅스 가자" 응원 관련 소동도 떠올리게 한다. 이준석 대선 후보가 스타벅스코리아의 2026년 5월 18일 '탱크데이' 텀블러 판촉을 1980년 5·18민주화운동에 대한 모욕으로 연결시키며 놀라운 "상상력"을 발휘했다. 많은 사람들이 이를 지나친 논리적 비약으로 봤다. 그럼에도 일부 정부 부처는 불매운동을 벌이기까지 했다. 스타벅스코리아의 모기업인 신세계그룹의 정용진 회장은 공개 사과했고, 경찰은 스타벅스코리아에 대해 압수수색을 진행했다. 배재고 팀은 5·18국립묘지를 방문해 응원에 대해 사과했다. 같은 기준이라면 이 영화의 감독, 배우 및 제작진들도 최소한 박정희 전 대통령 묘소를 방문해 추도하고 사과할 준비를 갖춰야 한다.

검증되지 않은 가설이 세련된 상업 영화의 힘을 통해 숨겨진 진실로 공중의식에 뿌리내릴 때의 위험은 심각하다. 영화적 상상력은 증거의 대체물이 될 수 없다. 허구가 확립된 역사적 사실, 특히 국가적 비극의 그럴듯한 설명으로 제시될 때, 역사 왜곡에 대한 비판은 불가피하다. 표현의 자유는 중요하다. 하지만 그것이 사실과 허구 사이의 경계를 흐릿하게 할 자유는 아니다. 최소한 제작진과 배급사는 박정희·육영수 유족들에게 사과하고, 이 영화가 확립된 역사적 사실을 묘사하지 않는다는 점을 관객들에게 명확히 해야 한다.

editorials.title: Fact vs. fiction
editorials.body: A controversial film hypothesis raises questions about historical distortion Controversy over “The Assassin(s),” a film about the 1974 shooting death of Yuk Young-soo, wife of then-President Park Chung-hee, has spilled into the political arena. At issue is not artistic license itself, but whether cinematic invention can justify distorting established historical facts. The film depicts the Aug. 15, 1974, shooting and advances a plot hypothesis that people close to Park or the Korean Central Intelligence Agency may have been involved. The filmmakers insist they did not explicitly identify who was behind the assassination. Yet the film invites audiences to entertain the insinuation that Park himself used or was involved in the incident to overcome a political crisis. For his children, the suggestion that their father may have been involved in their mother’s death to preserve his power is an especially grave insult. The historical record does not substantiate the theory. The Special Investigation Headquarters concluded at the time that Moon Se-kwang, acting on orders from North Korea and Jochongnyeon, the pro-Pyongyang federation of Korean residents in Japan, attempted to assassinate Park but missed, with a stray bullet striking and killing the first lady. Questions have been raised over the years, but no evidence has emerged to substantiate the claim that Park orchestrated his wife’s death. Rep. Joo Jin-woo of the opposition People Power Party criticized the film for portraying Park, rather than North Korea, as being behind Yuk’s assassination. He called it a historical distortion, not mere cinematic imagination, and said those involved should be punished. Party leader Jang Dong-hyeok called for a boycott, while Rep. Shin Dong-uk urged that screenings be halted. A former Seoul city council member also filed a criminal complaint against some production staff, accusing them of defaming Park. Yet the ruling Democratic Party of Korea has remained conspicuously silent. Why? Perhaps because the film is doing for the party what it has long done itself: denigrating Park. If a film had used a similarly shocking imagination to disparage former Presidents Kim Dae-jung or Roh Moo-hyun, would the Democratic Party have been so tolerant? It is difficult to imagine it would have been. The party pushed through a law imposing up to five years in prison for spreading false information about the May 18 Democratization Movement, which took place in its traditional stronghold of Jeonnam-Gwangju. Yet when a film raises an unverified theory about Park, the party has nothing to say. The contrast is glaring. It is a double standard. The controversy also recalls the uproar over the Paichai High School baseball team’s “Let’s go to Starbucks” chant during a June 29 game. President Lee Jae Myung lashed out at Starbucks Korea, displaying his remarkable “imagination” by linking its “Tank Day” tumbler promotion for May 18, 2026, with an insult to the May 18 Democratization Movement of 1980. Many saw this as an excessive leap in logic. Nevertheless, some government ministries went so far as to launch a boycott. Chung Yong-jin, chairman of Shinsegae Group, Starbucks Korea’s parent company, apologized publicly, while police conducted a search and seizure at Starbucks Korea. The Seoul-based Paichai team then visited the May 18 National Cemetery in Jeonnam-Gwangju to apologize for its chant. By the same standard, the film’s director, actors and other production staff should at least be prepared to visit Park Chung-hee’s grave, pay their respects and apologize. There is a serious danger when unverified hypotheses become embedded in the public consciousness as hidden truths through the power of a polished commercial film. Cinematic imagination is no substitute for evidence. When fiction is presented as a plausible explanation of established historical facts, especially a national tragedy, criticism of historical distortion is inevitable. Freedom of expression matters. But it is not a license to blur the line between fact and fiction. At the very least, the filmmakers and distributor should apologize to the bereaved family of Park and Yuk and make unmistakably clear to audiences that the film does not depict established historical fact. 검증되지 않은 가설이 세련된 상업 영화의 힘을 통해 숨겨진 진실로 공중의식에 뿌리내릴 때의 위험은 심각하다. 영화적 상상력은 증거의 대체물이 될 수 없다. 허구가 확립된 역사적 사실, 특히 국가적 비극의 그럴듯한 설명으로 제시될 때, 역사 왜곡에 대한 비판은 불가피하다. 표현의 자유는 중요하다. 하지만 그것이 사실과 허구 사이의 경계를 흐릿하게 할 자유는 아니다. 최소한 제작진과 배급사는 박정희·육영수 유족들에게 사과하고, 이 영화가 확립된 역사적 사실을 묘사하지 않는다는 점을 관객들에게 명확히 해야 한다.
